newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU's Legras defends wheat export warning.
newsitem.headline: EU's Legras defends wheat export warning.

text.p: The European Union's agriculture director on Monday reaffirmed that the EU may slow its wheat exports after exporters said they were sceptical about his previous warning about a slowdown.
"My statement was very reasonable," Guy Legras told Reuters by telephone from Brussels on Monday.
"I simply wanted to say that one cannot expect a free ride each Thursday," (when the EU holds weekly grain tenders), he said.

Legras, director general for agriculture at the European Commission, had told Reuters in Paris on Friday that the EU might "turn the screw on exports" after authorising export of more than one million tonnes of wheat in the previous two weeks.
He said this might happen at the next opportunity when the EU holds its weekly auction on December 19.

But exporters said they doubted that EU would tighten its grip on exports at what will be its last tender of the year. They noted that the EU has a large crop to sell at a time when there are plenty of buyers on the world market.
The EU's weekly export channel will be closed for two weeks over Christmas and New Year.
Legras gave no precise indication in either interview of how much wheat the EU hoped to export in coming weeks.
Chicago soft red winter wheat futures closed higher on Friday, supported partly by Legras' warning of a drop in wheat export volumes this week.
At its last tender on December 12, the EU awarded 477,700 tonnes of free-market soft wheat for export.
It also cleared around 550,000 tonnes of targeted wheat exports for Africa last week, grain officials said.
Legras said on Friday bids for over 1.3 million tonnes of EU wheat at the December 12 tender may have reflected efforts by a few traders to get hold of remaining wheat licences.
He also said the EU had already exported plenty of wheat this season (July/June) and there was no need to go too far. --Paris newsroom +331 4221 5146
